Series::is_mps¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

bool Series::is_mps() const noexcept

What It Does¶

Returns true when this Series currently lives on the MPS platform (Apple’s Metal Performance Shaders backend), false otherwise (CPU, or a different accelerator such as CUDA).

It is a metadata read — platform() == Platform::MPS — that never transfers data, never probes the machine, and cannot throw.

is_mps() is the strict, per-backend test, the MPS counterpart of is_cuda. It sits below is_gpu: every MPS Series is is_gpu(), but an accelerator Series on CUDA is is_gpu() and not is_mps(). Use is_mps() when the next step is MPS-specific — an MPS-only code path, or a fallback decision for an operation the MPS backend does not yet implement natively. When the branch is just “accelerator vs. CPU”, use is_gpu.

Whether the machine supports MPS at all is pluss::platform_available(pluss::pMPS) — check that before calling to(pluss::pMPS).

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

bool true iff platform() == Platform::MPS.

Gradient¶

Not applicable — is_mps() returns a plain bool.

Examples¶

Example 1. A fresh Series is on the CPU, so is_mps() is false.

auto x = pluss::series::zeros({2});
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "is_mps=" << x.is_mps()
          << " is_gpu=" << x.is_gpu() << "\n";

Output¶

is_mps=false is_gpu=false

Example 2. After to(pluss::pMPS) the predicate flips — and so does is_gpu, while is_cuda stays false. (Output from an Apple-Silicon host where MPS is available.)

auto x = pluss::series::zeros({2});
auto m = x.to(pluss::pMPS);
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "platform()=" << m.platform()
          << " is_cpu=" << m.is_cpu()
          << " is_gpu=" << m.is_gpu()
          << " is_cuda=" << m.is_cuda()
          << " is_mps=" << m.is_mps() << "\n";

Output¶

platform()=mps is_cpu=false is_gpu=true is_cuda=false is_mps=true

Example 3. Moving back to the CPU flips it all the way back.

auto x = pluss::series::zeros({2});
auto m = x.to(pluss::pMPS);
auto back = m.to(pluss::pCPU);
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "back: platform()=" << back.platform()
          << " is_mps=" << back.is_mps()
          << " is_cpu=" << back.is_cpu() << "\n";

Output¶

back: platform()=cpu is_mps=false is_cpu=true

x, m, and back are three independent Series; to() produces a new tensor and never mutates its receiver.

Example 4. Gate a transfer on pluss::platform_available(pluss::pMPS) so the same source runs on any host.

auto x = pluss::series::zeros({2});
if (pluss::platform_available(pluss::pMPS)) {
  auto m = x.to(pluss::pMPS);
  std::cout << "moved to MPS; is_mps=" << std::boolalpha << m.is_mps() << "\n";
} else {
  std::cout << "MPS unavailable; staying on CPU (is_mps=" << std::boolalpha
            << x.is_mps() << ")\n";
}

Output¶

moved to MPS; is_mps=true

is_mps() reports where a tensor is; platform_available(pMPS) reports whether the machine could put one there.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • is_mps() is strict: an accelerator Series on CUDA is not is_mps(). Use is_gpu for “on any accelerator”.

  • It reports this tensor’s placement, not machine capability — use pluss::platform_available(pluss::pMPS) before a transfer.

  • A binary op requires matching platforms; an MPS tensor cannot be combined with a CPU tensor directly (move one with to()).

  • Not every operation has a native MPS kernel; some fall back internally. is_mps() tells you the tensor is on MPS, not that every subsequent call stays there.

  • The predicate never transfers data and never throws.

Summary¶

is_mps() reports whether a Series currently resides on the MPS platform:

  • strict per-backend: platform() == Platform::MPS

  • a subset of is_gpu — every MPS tensor is is_gpu(), not vice versa

  • distinct from pluss::platform_available(pMPS) (a machine capability)

  • noexcept, metadata-only

See Also¶

  • Series::is_gpu: “on any accelerator” — the backend-agnostic branch.

  • Series::is_cuda: the other strict per-backend test.

  • Series::is_cpu: the exact complement of is_gpu().

  • Series::platform(): the underlying Platform value (cpu / cuda / mps).

  • Series::to: move a Series onto (or off) MPS.
